notes.title: Publisher Sale & Autumn Update Preview - Workshop 1.0 & New Decks
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We’re planning to release a new update next week. The long-awaited Workshop will finally make its debut! But since content driven by your creativity doesn’t quite feel like a “proper” update on its own, we’ve also pulled forward part of our roadmap and added two new decks: Gourd Mahjong and Imperial Edict Mahjong (originally “Divine Mahjong” on the roadmap), plus a brand-new Real-time Scoring system. This took us a bit more time than expected, and we truly appreciate your patience.

Also, starting September 15, we’ll be joining the XD Publisher Sale, [u][b]with 20% OFF for three weeks[/b][/u] until October 6, right through the Autumn Sale!


[h3]Workshop 1.0 Launch[/h3]

The long-anticipated Workshop is finally here! You can customize tiles, patterns, artifacts, and more with Lua. We’ll also provide technical documentation to help you create mods, and you’re welcome to join our Discord to get access.

In short, the Workshop lets you freely expand upon the current gameplay or even build entirely new material sets or artifact packs to make your own custom rules. We can’t wait to see what kind of creations you’ll come up with. And don’t forget to share your great works with the community!


[h3]New Decks: Gourd Mahjong & Imperial Edict Mahjong[/h3]

We’ve all had that frustrating moment: you are carefully crafting a build, only to have it crushed on a boss level that restricts suits or limits patterns. The Gourd Mahjong is here to let you turn the tables!

This deck starts with the exclusive artifact Purple Gold Gourd. Each time you defeat a boss, you can absorb its ability and make it your own. That means through the game, you can grow stronger and accumulate multiple boss abilities to unlock wild, unexpected combos. Combined with certain artifacts and patterns, this deck opens up countless crazy plays and unpredictable fun.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/e948b0f7a20b1efc47da48b4dd2d8cb63dee3b4d.gif[/img]
(Localization in Progress)

Ever felt the despair of a bad opening hand? As many players know, the very first play can set the tone for the entire game. A bad opening hand can really get in your mind. What if you could always start with a ready-made set?

That’s the core of the Imperial Edict Mahjong. Each round begins with a random set in your hand. This gives you more flexibility from the very start, making it easier for deckbuilding with a clear direction. 

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/eddf8fda2f538f10a5204ee711ecc4e78183c2c9.png[/img]
(Localization in Progress)

[h3]Real-time Scoring[/h3]

Many players have told us that the scoring felt a bit “delayed,” especially when multiple artifacts had synergies. It wasn’t always clear how much each artifact was contributing.

This update brings a Real-time Scoring system. For example, in the combo of Cinnabar Pen and Red Wood, tiles containing red immediately trigger the dyeing and Fan multiplying effects when played. Overall, score changes will now be more immediate and intuitive, helping you adjust your strategy on the fly.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/92b146f34a35a423b9fba947b5ab4ec9dffac737.gif[/img]
(Localization in Progress)

The new content is nearly complete and currently in the final QA stage. Please stay tuned for the exact update time and detailed patch notes in our next announcement. If you’d like to take part in testing, or if you have thoughts about this preview, feel free to join our official [url=https://discord.com/invite/F4Y5KCtg8F]Discord[/url] and share with us!


The Aotenjo Development Team

notes.title: July 31 Summer Update Preview - Dessert Tiles, Custom Tile Material Set
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We’re planning to release an update next week, introducing several new features outlined in our original Roadmap. These include the new Dessert Tiles, the Custom Tile Material Set feature, and gamepad support, which means now you can lean back and enjoy the game.

We’ve preserved many commonly used operations for gamepad users, and added additional convenience features tailored for gamepad play. However, gamepad support took slightly more time than expected to debug.

The new content is now fully developed and undergoing final QA. We aim to release the update early next week. Thank you for your patience and understanding. Please stay tuned for the exact update time and detailed patch notes in our upcoming announcements. This dev blog offers an early preview of the summer update.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/1f7b55094258a4d23bf821098533a6afc156633a.gif[/img]

[h3]New Tile Material: Dessert Tiles[/h3]
This new tile material was inspired by earlier food-themed artifacts like Xiaolongbao, Tanghulu, and Bubble Tea, the kind of designs that make you hungry while playing😋.

Dessert Tiles include five common materials: Chocolate, Mille-feuille, Sugar Cube, Lollipop, and Cheese; and two epic materials: Popsicle and Jelly. Compared to other tile materials, Dessert Tiles offer significantly higher scoring multipliers.

However, with higher rewards come more risks. Dessert Tiles introduce a special Freshness mechanic: each tile has a Freshness value that decreases at the end of each round if the tile remains in the Played Hand. When Freshness reaches 0, the tile loses its material. After all, desserts melting in summer is only natural😄.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/88cbb45c00f5e1224a2eed79e1082ca5c28ed2c8.gif[/img]

[h3]Custom Tile Material Set[/h3]
Each tile material in the game has distinct characteristics, but our players have never been limited to just one strategy. With this update, we’re introducing the Custom Tile Material Set feature, allowing you to freely assemble a set from all unlocked materials— any 5 common materials and 2 epic materials, across different sets.

We’re looking forward to seeing your creative combinations after the update. Don’t forget to share your favorite builds with the community.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/116c8085809e81e8b4dd8f8b38dd98ebbaa7409d.jpg[/img]
Additionally, we’ve also fixed several issues affecting gameplay.

If you have any feedback or suggestions, feel free to join our official [url=https://discord.com/invite/F4Y5KCtg8F]Discord[/url] server and communicate with us directly.

The Aotenjo Development Team

Our new Yin‑Yang deck draws inspiration from this scenario: a standard Sequence like 1‑2‑3 is called a “Yang Sequence,” and its counterpart, a jump Sequence like 1‑3‑5, is dubbed an “Yin Sequence.”

notes.content:
Greetings, fellow Mahjong enjoyers!

The April update we teased last week [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3066570/view/507326244048601598?l=english]here[/url] has finally dropped! [b]Artifacts[/b]

2.Fixed abnormal interaction between the Corrupt Crystal Ball Artifact and Mo Tiles.
3.Fixed the bug that Bamboo Shoot Artifact was triggering under unwanted conditions.

notes.title: “Spring Update” Content Preview
notes.content:
Hello, fellow mahjong fans! After an intense sprint of bug fixing and fine-tuning, we’re happy to report that the game is more stable than ever. With the current build feeling rock‑solid, our team has shifted gears full‑steam into the April update, which is targeting a roll‑out before May 1st. Below is an early look at what’s coming your way.

Additionally, at the invitation of the IndieArk Strategems Fest and the Steam China Eastern Game Fest, we will be having a two-week 12% OFF discount from April 22 to May 6.

[h2][b]🌳 New Wooden Tile Material[/b][/h2]
Just in time for spring, we’re introducing [b]Wooden Tiles[/b]! Unlike Mineral Tiles that boost your score, Porcelain Tiles with their sleek shine, or the risky‑high‑reward Monster Tiles, [b]Wooden Tiles[/b] reward clever discards and [b]Forced Discards[/b]. You’ll find five standard variants (e.g., [b]Nanmu Wood, Ghostwood, or Mistwood[/b]) and two epic variants, plus over a dozen exclusive artifacts. Chain reactions are the name of the game here: each discard can snowball into strategic mayhem. We can’t wait to see how you experiment with them!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/7112a9fe0bed26041bde19a7d6879db34d82db86.gif[/img]

[h2][b]🎲 Dozens of Fresh Entry Events[/b][/h2]
To crank up the roguelike excitement, we’ve not only tweaked difficulty‑based buffs and debuffs at the start of each run, but also expanded our Entry Events from the original eight to over twenty. Expect more “high‑risk, high‑reward” scenarios right from your first hand. Whether you’re craving a wild advantage or a brutal challenge, there’s now even more variety in how you kick off your playthroughs.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/267362f9e1ef890746f28330ab94219b1c7f64ba.png[/img]
[h2][b]🔧 Artifact Crafting System[/b][/h2]
A bunch of you mentioned that in the late‑run, Artifacts can feel underwhelming compared to the early game. We heard you! In addition to rebalancing existing items, we’re rolling out a brand‑new [b]Artifact Crafting System[/b]. Now you can combine transitional or niche Artifacts into powerful hybrids with multiple effects. This not only raises the power ceiling but also helps keep your inventory tidy. No more cluttered Artifact list!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/cf7ecdd875a65aa5a8e082a60db4e544aa3c7f5a.gif[/img]

[h2][b]🎉 Extra Goodies & Polish[/b][/h2]
Of course, no update would be complete without some universal Artifact and Gadget additions, plus an epic boss‑battle theme track to amp up those final showdowns. 

[b]How to Get Involved[/b]
All of the new content is largely built and now in final QA. Stay tuned here or on our roadmap for the exact drop time and full patch notes. If you’d like early access, hop into our official Discord for playtesting. And don’t be shy with feedback! We’re always humbled by your support and ideas.
Thank you for playing and growing with us. We couldn’t do this without you!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45104517/2a2e8162d00cd69c04b3aac0f00b7b55ba2945f9.png[/img]
Our Discord Channel：[url=https://discord.gg/UwBzpBEGPH]https://discord.gg/UwBzpBEGPH[/url]

The Aotenjo Development Team

notes.content:
Hello, fellow mahjong enjoyers! We have just released an update that adds hotkeys for gadgets and popup for keywords, along with various adjustments and fixes to improve your gaming experience. If you encounter any issues while playing, please feel free to share your feedback on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/FMTMJz3UJN]Discord[/url]. We will address them as soon as possible.
Additionally, [u][b]the game will kick off a one-week 12% OFF Spring Sale from March 13 to March 20 (UTC-8).[/b][/u]

[b]V.0.2.3.1-EA PATCH NOTES[/b]
[h3]Newly Added[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Added gadgets hotkeys: You can now press the keyboard's number keys to use gadgets.
[*] Added keywords popup: Players can now read the detailed explanation by hovering their mouse over the keywords in different colors.
[/olist]
[h3]Adjustments[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Artifact “Golden Scissors”: Effect also triggers at the end of a round.
[*] Artifact “Ancient Scripture”: Effect adjusted from 16/32 Fu to 20/40 Fu.
[*] Gadget “Red Marker”: Marks left will be counted as green under the effect of Artifact “3D Glasses”.
[*] Gadget “Magnet”: Directional marks will now factor into the color determination on the Tiles.
[*] Location “Rubble Pile”: Now in late game, the probability of rare or epic Artifacts appearing will slightly decrease.
[*] Pattern “Pure Outside Hand”: Base Fan adjusted from 48 to 36.
[*] Pattern “All Fives”: Base/growth Fan adjusted from 64/48 to 48/36.
[*] Pattern “Triple Triplet”: Growth Fan adjusted from 6 to 8.
[*] Pattern “Triple Resonated Triplet”: Base/growth Fan adjusted from 48/38 to 64/36.
[*] Pattern “Mixed Shifted Triplets”: Base/growth Fan adjusted from 24/16 to 36/24.
[*] Pattern “Mirrored Triplets”: Base Fan adjusted from 88 to 108.
[*] Pattern category icons: adjusted to now only visible in detailed information mode.
[/olist]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Fixed a bug where, under certain circumstances, the interaction between “Mo Tiles” and the Artifact “Spray of Malice” causes the game to freeze.
[*] Fixed a bug where the simultaneous presence of “Mo Tiles” and the Artifact “Burning Pact” causes the game to freeze.
[*] Fixed a bug where ending the game in specific situations resulted in incorrect entries in the history log.
[*] Fixed a bug where skipping a turn could cause the Artifact “Pirate's Treasure Chest” to exceed 100 stacks.
[*] Fixed the incorrect interaction between the Artifact “Frog Amulet” and "Mo Tiles" by changing the trigger timing of "Frog Amulet" to occur after discarding.
[*] Fixed a bug where "Schemer Mahjong" displayed an incorrect description when advanced to Axe difficulty.
[*] Fixed a bug where when transforming a single "Mysterious Color Porcelain Tile” into  "Famille Verte Porcelain Tile", it doesn’t properly acquire the "Famille Verte Porcelain Tile" bonus.
[*] Fixed a bug where "Mysterious Color Porcelain Tile" did not trigger the scoring effect when transforming into "Blue and White Porcelain".
[*] Fixed a bug where the Full House keyword did not correctly display its associated description.
[*] Fixed a bug where "Taotie Tile" and "Nest Tile" caused the game to freeze in certain situations.
[*] Fixed a bug where the Artifact "Golden Scissors" could alter the material of Flower Tiles.
[*] Fixed various description errors and localization texts.
[/olist]

notes.title: (Updated) Update Preview - Increased Initial Discard Limit & Boss Adjustments
notes.content:
Hello, Mahjong enthusiasts! It has been over two weeks since our game launched, and even during the Lunar New Year, our team has been hard at work. We’ve carefully read and discussed every piece of community feedback and reviews.
Instead of making scattered minor adjustments, we wanted to take a more structured approach to ensure noticeable improvements to your gameplay experience. Later today, we will roll out an update focusing on [b][u]core game mechanics, corruption mechanics, and boss adjustments[/u][/b]—areas frequently mentioned in community discussions. The update is currently in its final testing phase, and since it is quite substantial, we welcome players to join our discord to provide feedback.

📌[b]Increased Initial Discard Chances to 10[/b]
We've noticed that for most players, the frustration of being unable to make a move far outweighs the disappointment of failing to achieve a high score. Even with consumable items, extreme cases still exist where bad luck can force a round-ending pass despite optimal deck-building and decision-making. T[b]o reduce[/b] the impact of luck, we have increased the initial discard limit to 10.

📌[b]Smoother Score Progression Curve[/b]
Beyond reducing randomness, we have been closely monitoring feedback on difficulty levels, especially regarding the "Goose" difficulty tier. The gap between the base difficulty and Goose was too significant, making Goose feel like an insurmountable wall. To address this, [u][b]we have reduced the score requirement increase for Goose difficulty by 30%[/b][/u] to create a smoother progression.

Additionally, to improve the core game design,[u][b] patterns that have not been unlocked will now contribute 50% of their original multiplier when successfully played[/b][/u] instead of granting no bonus at all. This prevents discouragement when discovering new patterns for the first time. Furthermore, the prices of previously unpurchased Artifacts in the shop have been reduced to prevent minor financial setbacks from hindering gameplay progression.

📌[b]Boss Adjustments & Corruption Mechanic Update[/b]
We have adjusted six bosses, including Immaculate, Colorless, and Heartless:
[list]
[*] [b]Flawless[/b]: The effect that halves the multiplier of hands missing a specific pattern category (Wind, Forest, Fire, Mountain) has been temporarily removed. We plan to reintroduce this challenge in higher difficulty settings where it will be a known endgame boss rather than an unexpected hurdle for newer players.
[*] [b]Colorless:[/b] The previous effect of "all tiles fade when played" was too universally punishing. It has now been permanently removed and replaced with a new effect that provides a more strategic challenge specifically targeting red-themed builds.
[*] [b]Heartless[/b]: Its effect has been changed from "all non-terminal pair tiles corrupt when played" to "if your pair tile is not a terminal, this play is corrupted." This adjustment allows for more strategic play without arbitrarily punishing all builds.
[/list]
Regarding corruption mechanics, we previously mentioned our goal of preserving corruption-based builds rather than outright removing them. The issue with the old corruption mechanic was that it altered tiles mid-game, affecting discard choices. The updated version now cleanses the corruption effect when a corrupted tile is discarded, synergizing well with the increased discard limit and providing an effective countermeasure in the late-game Endless Mode, where discards are abundant.

More detailed updates and changes are listed below:

————————————————
[b]V0.2.2.0-EA PATCHNOTE[/b]
[b]New Features & Improvements[/b]
[olist]
[*] New Artifacts: Added "Observer," "Dragon Codex," "Travel Bag," "Indigo Pen," "Burning Pact," and more.
[*] Stage Details Panel: Players can now view their current game progress both in and out of rounds, including upcoming boss restrictions (click the stage name to view details).
[*] In-game Tips for New Players: Added tips in Zhou's Store to help players understand the system quicker.
[*] Hold-to-Skip Toggle: A new setting to prevent accidental skipping or double-taps.
[*] Stackable Artifact Counters: Artifacts that accumulate stacks now display their current count directly on their icons.
[/olist]
[b]Optimizations[/b]
[olist]
[*] The game will now continue running when minimized.
[*] Ultra-wide screen support added—UI and hand displays are now properly aligned.
[*] Previously undiscovered patterns can now be viewed in the collections menu.
[*] When owning the "Void Stele" Artifact, epic and legendary patterns successfully played will now be marked in the collections menu.
[/olist]
[b]Balance Adjustments
Boss Adjustments:[/b]
[olist]
[*] Flawless: Temporarily removed the effect that halves multipliers for missing pattern categories.
[*] Unrest: Removed the effect that increases score targets by 40% for all subsequent rounds (Unrest can finally rest in peace).
[*] Colorless: Removed the "all played tiles fade" effect.
[*] Heartless: Adjusted corruption condition to only trigger if the pair tile is not a terminal.
[*] Unyielding: Adjusted its effect from "each duplicate tile increases target score by 4%" to "each duplicate tile increases target score by 5%."
[*] New Boss: "Unred" - Tiles containing red will now increase the target score by 6% when played.
[/olist]
[b]Artifact Adjustments:[/b]
[olist]
[*][b] 3D Glasses[/b]: Rarity downgraded from Rare → Common.
[*] [b]Copper Pocket Watch:[/b] Rarity downgraded from Rare → Common.
[*] [b]Demon Statue[/b]: Rarity downgraded from Epic → Rare.
[*] [b]Pruner[/b]: Effect changed from "permanently reduces 3 symbols each use" → "permanently reduces 2 symbols each use."
[*] [b]Collector's Amulet:[/b] Multiplier increased from x0.75 → x1.0.
[*] [b]Corrupted Crystal Ball:[/b] Bonus per Nest Tile increased from x0.05 → x0.1.
[*] [b]Fire Axe:[/b] New Effect - Grants an additional 80 symbols if it provides 20x or more multiplier.
[*] [b]Copper Dagger:[/b] Bonus per bronze item increased from 25 symbols → 30 symbols.
[*] [b]Brush:[/b] Recoloring chance increased from 1/13 → 1/8, now capable of restoring color to faded tiles.
[*] [b]Guzheng:[/b] Now removes all negative effects from previously played tiles instead of only the currently playing tile.
[*] [b]Pirate Chest:[/b] Now prevents further accumulation of pirate coins when full.
[*] [b]Agate Dagger[/b]: Bonus per agate tile increased from x0.05 → x0.1.
[*] [b]Tricolor Flower[/b]: Effect increased from +2x multiplier per trigger → +3x.
[*] [b]Kaleidoscope[/b]: Multiplier increased from x2 → x3.
[*] [b]Shredder[/b]: Improved rewards when deleting epic/legendary patterns.
[*] [b]Frog Amulet[/b]: Reworked Effect - Discarding a non-simple tile now destroys it (limit: 3 times per round).
[*] [b]Vermilion Bird Fan[/b]: Reworked Effect - Expended Artifacts grant a x2 multiplier to hands, and depleted non-consumable items grant a x1.2 multiplier.
💬Dev：[i]The original design encouraged players to discard all items early, lowering game adaptability. The new version retains the "Empty Castle" concept while fostering synergy with more Artifacts and items.[/i]
[*] We have also increased the rate of finding rare Artifacts in East Wind Circle Liulang Hall.
[/olist]
[b]Pattern Adjustments[/b]
[olist]
[*] [b][Buffed] All Five, All Big-Medium-Small[/b] base/bonus values: [b]48/36 → 64/48[/b]
Reason: Adjusted to match other epic-level comprehensive patterns.
[*] [b][Nerfed] Seven Pairs[/b] growth value: [b]48 → 24[/b]
💬Dev：[i]Reducing its overpowered mid-game performance, encouraging players to mix it with other patterns for specialized builds.[/i]
[*] [b][Buffed] Symmetrical Tiles[/b] bonus value: [b]24 → 32[/b]
[*] [b][Adjusted] All Terminals And Honors[/b] base/bonus values: [b]32/32 → 36/24[/b]
 Reason: Strengthened early-game performance while reducing abnormal upgrade scaling.
[*] [b][Buffed] Small Four Winds[/b] base value: [b]108 → 128[/b]
 Reason: Adjusted to match other four-meld patterns.
[*] [b][Buffed] Three Triplets[/b] bonus value: [b]6 → 8[/b]
💬Dev：[i]While triplet-based patterns shouldn’t scale as well as sequence-based ones, the previous growth rate of 6 points per level was too weak compared to other blue-tier patterns. This update compensates by improving the growth value of high-rarity triplet patterns, ensuring they remain dominant when fully built.[/i]
[*] [b][Buffed] Four Triplets[/b] bonus value: [b]24 → 32[/b]
[*] [b][Buffed] Three Kans[/b] bonus value: [b]24 → 32[/b]
[*] [b][Buffed] Tile Hog+[/b] base value: [b]12 → 16[/b]
[*] [b][Buffed] Three Dragons Pairs[/b] base value: [b]48 → 68[/b]
[*] [b][Buffed] Thirteen Orphans[/b] upgrade bonus: [b]188 → 248[/b]
Reason: Compensating for the low base value due to its lack of synergy with other patterns.
[*] [b][Buffed] Mixed/Pure Double Sequence, Short Straight, All Sequences[/b] upgrade bonus: [b]1.5 → 2[/b]
[i]Reason: Strengthening the growth potential of the "Book of the Forest" pattern pack and improving mid-game curve for sequence-based builds.[/i]
[*] [b][Adjusted] Twice Pure Double Sequence[/b] base/upgrade bonus: 48/68 → 68/48
Reason: Preventing an excessively large jump from Lv.1 to Lv.2.
[*] [b][Buffed] Pure Triple Sequences[/b] base value: [b]58 → 68[/b]
[*] [b][Buffed] Three-Suited Terminal Sequences[/b] Meeting upgrade bonus: [b]88 → 128[/b]
Reason: Rewarding the high-risk Twin Dragon strategy.
[*] [b][Buffed] Half Flush[/b] upgrade bonus: [b]2 → 3[/b]
Reason: Smoothing the mid-game transition for character/terminal flush builds.
[*] [b][Buffed] Mirror Triplets[/b] base/upgrade bonus: [b]68/88 → 88/58[/b]
Reason: Strengthening niche triplet-based strategies.
[*] [b][Buffed] No Reds[/b] upgrade bonus: [b]16 → 24[/b]
Reason: Adjusting to match standard rare patterns and reinforcing the Faded style.
[*] [b][Buffed] Big Seven Stars[/b] base/upgrade bonus: [b]188/188 → 218/168[/b]
Reason: Compensating for its lack of synergy with other patterns.
[*] [b][Buffed] Ao no Domon[/b] base value: [b]48 → 68[/b]
Reason: Adjusted to match its difficulty level.
[*] [b][Nerfed] Three-Suited Character Sequences[/b] base/upgrade bonus: [b]68/48 → 58/38[/b]
[/olist]
[b]Other Adjustments[/b]
[olist]
[*] [b][Buffed] A Pack of Tools Event:[/b] Now grants two random tools (previously three random gadgets).
[*] [b][Buffed] Schemer Mahjong:[/b] Now grants[b] 10 discard chances at East - East[/b] (Stage 1) as usual.
[*][b] [Nerfed] Malice Sawmill:[/b] Increased card removal cost thresholds from[b] 110/85/60 → 110/90/70 [/b]remaining tiles.
Reason: Since the initial discard count per round has been increased by 5, this change balances the impact on smaller hands.
[*] [b][Adjusted] Colorless Effect:[/b] [b]-5 Fu → -3 Fu[/b]
[*][b] [Adjusted] Corruption Effect: -0.5/-2/-4/-6 Fan → -1/-2/-6/-12 Fan[/b]
💬Dev：[i]Since Corruption can be easily cleansed by discarding, its penalty has been increased to balance its impact while improving the rewards from Demon Statues.[/i]
[*] [b][Buffed] Bone Porcelain Tile[/b]: Maximum fan increase limit [b]removed[/b] (previously capped at 20 fan).
[*] [b][Buffed] Pink Porcelain Tile:[/b] Score multiplier per unique tile increased dynamically: [b]+1 → +1/2/3/4 [/b]based on game progression.
[*] [b][Buffed] Increased the chance of encountering rare gadgets in Treasure Shop.[/b]
[*] [b][Buffed] Flower Tiles: Farming now permanently grants +10 Fu to the playing pair as well.[/b]
[/olist]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[olist]
[*] Fixed a bug where gadget usage count could go below 0.

notes.title: Aotenjo 01- 23 Update Patch Note
notes.content:
Greetings, everyone!

Aotenjo has been live for four days, and we’re incredibly grateful for all your support and encouragement!
Over the past few days, the team has been actively collecting and reviewing your feedback. With the weekend approaching — we have just released a [b]major update [/b]to address and optimize some of the key issues that have surfaced.

As we’ve mentioned before, our top priority is ensuring the best experience for current players. For this update, we’re focusing on simplifying the [b]Green Mahjong[/b] flow to prevent new players from getting stuck on certain mechanics or bosses before fully grasping the game.
[b]Patch notes for version 0.2.1.6 are at the end of this post for easy reference[/b]. If you encounter any issues, please join our[url=https://discord.gg/FMTMJz3UJN] official Discord community[/url] and send us your feedback.

[h3]About the Corruption Mechanic[/h3]
One of the most-discussed topics has been the [b]Corruption Mechanic[/b], particularly its effect in Endless Mode. Many players have pointed out that certain boss traits, combined with the mechanic, rely too heavily on luck rather than strategy.
While removing the mechanic altogether is a straightforward solution, we’re exploring adjustments first. We have some ideas for improvements, and you can expect changes in the [b]next update[/b].

[h3]Upcoming Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Level Details Page[/b]: View your current progress and upcoming level requirements at any time outside of a match.
[*] [b]New Artifacts[/b]: Adding a batch of exciting new Artifacts to enrich your strategy.
[*] [b]Music Toggle[/b]: For our veteran players who loved the 8-bit pixel music from earlier versions, we’re introducing a toggle option to switch between music styles.
[*] Add a Hold-to-Skip Option in settings, allowing players to long-press instead of clicking to skip 
[/list]
[h3]Version 0.2.1.6 Patch Notes[/h3]
[b][New Features][/b]
[olist]
[*] Added a display for remaining tiles when hovering over Mahjong tiles outside of matches.discarding tiles.
[/olist]
[b][Adjustments][/b]
[olist]
[*] [b]Boss: Flawless[/b] will no longer appear in Green Mahjong.
[*] Boss “[b]Unaided[/b]” effect now reduces the score multiplier of [b]Rare/Epic Artifacts[/b] to [b]x0.8/x0.7[/b] (was x0.8/x0.6).
[*] [b]Artifact: Gold Ingot[/b] multiplier reduced from[b] x3 to x2.5[/b] for single-suit numbered tiles.
[*] [b]Artifact: Bamboo Shoot[/b] effect now applies to tiles with a face value below 4 and [b]containing green color[/b].
[*] [b]Artifact: Jade Mirror[/b] multiplier per layer increased from 0.15 to 0.20.
[*] [b]Artifact: Brush[/b] rarity downgraded from Rare to Common.
[*] [b]Artifact: Mysterious Fleshball[/b] rarity downgraded from Rare to Common.
[/olist]
[b][Bug Fixes][/b]
[olist]
[*] Fixed an issue where [b]Copper Dagger[/b] did not apply to Copper tiles.
[*] Resolved a bug where combining [b]Mo Tiles[/b] and [b]Demon Tiles[/b] under certain conditions caused the game to crash.
[*] Corrected an issue where the upgraded [b]Origami Bear Artifact[/b] was mistakenly classified as Rare by the “Unaided” trait.
[*] Fixed cases where dragging Artifacts could result in a crash.
[/olist]
[h3]Join the Community![/h3]
Be sure to join our [url=https://discord.gg/FMTMJz3UJN]official Discord community[/url] to discuss strategies, and participate in playtests. We always read your feedback and look forward to chat with you!

[h3]Community Highlights[/h3]
We’ve received many guide submissions from players, and we’re excited to share some of them with you. Feel free to join our [url=https://discord.gg/FMTMJz3UJN]discord[/url] to exchange tips and tricks!
Don’t forget that our [b]Daily Score Sharing[/b] and [b]Community Tournament[/b] events are still ongoing! High scores continue to roll in, and we’re amazed by everyone’s creativity and mastery.

notes.title: 3 Days to Launch – Tips for New Players!
notes.content:
Hey Mahjong Masters!

The launch of Aotenjo: Infinite Hands is just around the corner—only 3 days to go! Mark your calendars: the game officially releases [u][b]on Monday, the 20th, at 11 AM (UTC+8)[/b][/u]—no delays, we promise!

In our last dev blog, we shared details about the [b]Early Access launch[/b] and our [b]2025 update roadmap[/b]. This time, we want to introduce some [b]handy tips[/b] for new players! While Aotenjo is a [b]mahjong-inspired roguelike deckbuilder[/b], [b]it doesn’t[/b] require deep mahjong knowledge to enjoy. The mechanics are designed to be approachable, and you’ll pick them up as you play!

[h3]Which Mahjong Should I Start With?[/h3]
We highly recommend starting with [b]Green Mahjong[/b]. It has a streamlined rule set, a built-in tutorial, and [b]5 extra discards[/b] (we’ll explain these later). The difficulty is also relatively low, making it the perfect starting point.
Once you’ve mastered Green Mahjong, you’ll unlock more complex styles! The [b]Early Access version [/b]includes six mahjong types: [b]Green, Blue, Galaxy, Bamboo, Rainbow, and Schemer Mahjong[/b]—each with unique mechanics and challenges!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/66455a758fb4a7db505c83cc755ad738455c9857.png[/img]

[h3]The Goal: Score! Score! And More Score![/h3]
The core gameplay is simple:
[olist]
[*] [b]Each round[/b], add new tiles to your hand and [b]score points[/b] based on your tile combinations.
[*] After [b]four rounds[/b], your total score determines whether you clear the level.
[*] Any [b]points beyond the required target [/b]convert into in-game [b]currency[/b]—which you can [b]spend on upgrades[/b] in the rest phase.
[/olist]
Just like traditional mahjong, Aotenjo is about [b]planning, adapting, and maximizing your score[/b]. So don’t hold back—aim for big hands and rack up those points!

[h3]Scoring System[/h3]
Scoring in Aotenjo follows a system[b] similar to classic mahjong: Base Points × Multipliers.[/b]
[b]Base Points (符, Fu)[/b]

Each tile has a fixed score value, and here’s an easy way to remember them:
[list]
[*] [b]Character, Bamboo, and Dot tiles:[/b]
[b]1 & 9 = 9 Fu, 2 & 8 = 8 Fu, 3 & 7 = 7 Fu, 4 & 6 = 6 Fu, 5 = 5 Fu[/b]
[*] [b]Honor tiles (East, South, West, North, Red, Green, White) = 10 Fu[/b]
[/list]
(Don’t worry if you can’t memorize this! You can always [b]hover over tiles in-game[/b] to check their Fu value.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/9c29c668feea7e0275ee1c7d5d225617660a6bdb.png[/img]
[h3]Multipliers (番, Fan)[/h3]
Fan comes from specific [b]tile combinations[/b]—these are called [b]Patterns (番种, Yakus).[/b]
You might recognize famous ones like [b]Full Flush (清一色) [/b]and [b]Thirteen Orphans (十三幺)[/b]—the rarer and harder a pattern is to complete, the[b] higher the multiplier![/b]

Unlike traditional mahjong, in Aotenjo, you can [b]upgrade your patterns[/b] by purchasing[b] Pattern Books[/b], increasing their fan and [b]boosting your score potential![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/fae6fc9bb5d83007887d482b35792f3fc5760959.png[/img]
To sum it up:
[list]
[*] [b]Discard low-value or unwanted tiles[/b]
[*] [b]Keep high-Fu tiles[/b]
[*] [b]Aim for high-Fan pattern[/b]
[/list]
Master this, and you’ll be on your way to victory!


[h3]Gadget Guide: “Rigging” Your Hand (Legally!)[/h3]
Sometimes, no matter how hard you try, [b]your tiles just won’t come together.[/b] That’s where Aotenjo's [b]special items[/b] come in!
These items can[b] temporarily modify tile values, suits, or even grant unique effects[/b]—making them invaluable for crafting powerful hands. For example:
[list]
[*] "[b]Cooked Rice[/b]": Temporarily reduces the number value of a Dot or Bamboo tile by 1.
[/list]
Use these wisely to [b]turn the tide [/b]in your favor!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/ae7911b878101460028f36f9d9a7af85c69bebe1.gif[/img]

[h3]Money Power 1: Map Locations[/h3]
Another way to [b]optimize your deck[/b] is by making [b]permanent changes[/b] to your [b]wall (your entire deck of tiles)[/b]. At the end of each round, you can choose [b]different locations[/b] to visit, each offering unique benefits:
[list]
[*] [b]Malice-Sawmill:[/b] Spend money to [b]remove unwanted tiles[/b] from your deck.
[*] [b]Bamboo Forest:[/b] Buy [b]new tiles [/b]to add to your deck.
[*] [b]Howling Mountain[/b]: Spend money to [b]enchant tiles[/b] with special effects.
[*] [b]Wan's Treasure Shop[/b]: Purchase [b]useful gadgets[/b] for your run.
[/list]
Your [b]currency is key [/b]to shaping your deck—so choose your path carefully!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/220d537785d5417ec6e44e2a64af0ddd53e9fb94.png[/img]
[h3]Money Power 2: The Store[/h3]
Artifacts are powerful items that provide permanent buffs throughout your run. They can:
[list]
[*] Boost Pattern multipliers
[*] Increase overall scoring potential
[*] Evolve specific tiles
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/93eb5874262cdc4b5477898de69c3706c9e76bb8.png[/img]
At the [b]Artifact Shop[/b], you can buy [b]various Artifacts[/b]—rarer ones cost more but provide stronger effects!
Additionally,[b] Pattern Packs [/b]are a great way to[b] level up your patterns[/b], unlocking [b]rare multipliers [/b]and enhancing your strategy. We recommend [b]prioritizing the Pattern Packs that match your preferred playstyle![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/dbb0a8668df3738b7d64fbee1c72e719103e2c57.png[/img]
[h3]Final Developer Tips[/h3]
Unlike traditional mahjong, where you need to form a [b]complete 14-tile hand,[/b] Aotenjo breaks it down into[b] four rounds.[/b] In each round:
[list]
[*] You[b] play a Triplet/Sequence + a Pair[/b] per turn.
[*] [b]The previous Pair is replaced each turn[/b]—use this to cycle out unwanted tiles.
[/list]
Some [b]pro strategies[/b] to keep in mind:
[olist]
[*] [b]Your final move is crucial! [/b]Each turn scores points, but the [b]last turn includes ALL previous tiles, so set up for big Pattern early[/b] and cash in at the end!
[*] [b]Use the Pair slot strategically[/b]—discard unwanted tiles by playing them as Pair in early turns to set up [b]a strong hand for the final Play.[/b]
[*] [b]You don’t necessarily need Malice-Sawmill to remove tiles! [/b]Some [b]items and artifacts [/b]can [b]shrink your deck[/b], helping you focus on key tiles faster.
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/e2f60a559c4915fcb99d2716ce1230a405a81cce.png[/img]
[h3]Join the Community[/h3]
To all our [b]closed beta and open test players—[/b]thank you for your support! We’d love for you to [b]share your own gameplay tips in the comments[/b] and in our [url=https://discord.gg/FMTMJz3UJN]Official Discord[/url].

[h3]Launch Discount![/h3]
Aotenjo: Infinite Hands will launch with a [u][b]12% discount for the first two weeks at $8.71 USD! [/b][/u]

notes.title: Early Access Release Date, What to Expect & 2025 Roadmap
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

It’s hard to believe that six months have passed since we first shared Aotenjo with our players. Since then, we've had a public demo, participated in the Steam Next Fest, and undergone multiple revisions and internal tests—all thanks to your valuable feedback! The game has evolved significantly from its early days, and we sincerely appreciate all the players who have supported and provided feedback.

In our last update, we mentioned that we were working hard to release the game before the Lunar New Year. Now, with the final build submitted for review, we’re excited to officially announce that Aotenjo will launch [u][b]in Early Access on January 19th (Sunday) at 7:00 PM PST[/b][/u]!

To celebrate, we’ve also released a brand-new trailer featuring our updated UI and our new name:
[previewyoutube=iW1pfmXb36M;full][/previewyoutube]
Don’t forget to add Aotenjo to your Steam Wishlist to stay updated and be notified when it goes live:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3066570/_/

[h2]What’s Included in the Early Access Version?[/h2]
After half a year of development, Aotenjo has come a long way from its original demo. Many of you might be wondering: How much content will be in the EA version?

To put it simply:[u][b] The Early Access version will have roughly three times the content of the previous demo.[/b][/u]

We’ve shared many of these updates in our previous dev logs:
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3066570/view/507315473246846998?l=english][Dev Log #3] UI Overhaul, New Decks & Bosses[/url]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3066570/view/4685521773540177366?l=english][Dev Log #2] Bamboo Mahjong, Porcelain Tiles & Advanced Difficulty[/url]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3066570/view/4356754561281185319?l=english][Dev Log #1] Developer FAQ[/url]

Since Aotenjo is a roguelike deck-building game themed around mahjong, pure content volume isn’t the only measure of its depth. By launching in Early Access, we aim to provide[b] a solid core gameplay experience with strong replayability[/b], while continuously refining and expanding the game.

We’ve spent a lot of time fine-tuning the strategic depth of Aotenjo:
[list]
[*] Each deck has its own unique theme and mechanics
[*] Encourages players to experiment with different builds and adapt strategies dynamically
[*] Boss fights are designed to challenge your tactics—not just your stats
[/list]
[h2]Future Updates & 2025 Roadmap[/h2]
As fellow Steam players, we understand the concerns about games that enter Early Access but are never fully released. That’s why we’ve carefully planned our development roadmap to give you a clear picture of what’s ahead.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/51bb249db5d0e980648aa2f2dea2e646eb080eee.png[/img]

Beyond regular bug fixes and balance adjustments, we will roll out [u][b]major content updates every 1-2 months[/b][/u] until we reach our vision for version 1.0, which includes:
[list]
[*] 16 fully developed decks, complete with unique relics and events

notes.title: Pre-Holiday Launch Sprint | Devlog #3 — UI Overhaul, New Decks, and Bosses
notes.content:
Hello Mahjong enthusiasts!

It’s been over a month since the Steam Next Fest, and we’ve been hard at work gathering feedback from every survey and player comments on the demo. We've been diving into a new development cycle and organized another closed beta test in our community to fine-tune some of the updates. Huge thanks to everyone who participated in the demo and the closed beta test — every piece of feedback has been an incredible motivation and help to the team!

We’re thrilled to share that most of the Early Access content is now complete, and [b]we’re sprinting toward a pre-Lunar New Year release.[/b] In this Dev Blog, let’s take a look at what’s been happening in Aotenjo!

[h2]UI Overhaul[/h2]
First up is the most noticeable change:[b] a full overhaul of the game’s UI![/b] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/27edd2ca67f2e5804e4f016c55834804f23e57bc.png[/img]
Since the game includes plenty of descriptions for gadgets, rules, and effects, here are what we have done:
[list]
[*] Replaced the plain monochrome backgrounds with more engaging visuals and restructured the layout to better prioritize information.
[*] Switched to a cleaner, more readable font. 
[*] You can now hover your mouse over gadgets to instantly see their effects on your hand.
[*] When selecting a tile, the score information will display clearly at the top, helping players optimize their builds. 
[*] In addition to drag-and-drop functionality, items can now also be used with a simple click.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/dd111c5588d25e7e9861c1653bb968c9f9240602.gif[/img]
[h2]Evolving Tutorial[/h2]
From unique rules to countless Mahjong tiles and quirky gadget effects, Aotenjo has always had a "complex" vibe since its first demo. Making the game accessible to Mahjong beginners remains one of our biggest challenges.

The tutorial in the Next Fest demo introduced basic gameplay mechanics, but we found that the Mahjong-specific terminology left some players, especially those new to Mahjong, feeling confused. In November’s closed beta, we expanded the tutorial with more detailed explanations of Mahjong terms, as well as the game’s overall flow and objectives. However, this led to a new problem: the sheer volume of information at once overwhelmed many players (oops :(
Now, we’re pivoting to a more practical approach. Instead of delivering a lecture-style tutorial, we’ll integrate lessons directly into gameplay. This way, players can learn when they are playing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/6803edbb2595bfabe415a01ee18385e00ed09fa8.png[/img]
[h2]New Decks, Gadgets, and Bosses[/h2]
Content-wise, we’ve been keeping the pace up! Following the [b]Bamboo Mahjong[/b] from the demo and [b]Rainbow Mahjong[/b] introduced in the beta, we’ve now completed [b]two additional decks[/b] for the EA version: [b]Galaxy Mahjong and Sneaky Mahjong[/b], each with their own unique gadgets, tiles, and rules.

[i]Rainbow Mahjong:
In traditional Mahjong, flower tiles such as the 4 seasons and the 4 flowers can be added to decks optionally to add variety, making the potential score higher and more fun. [/i]

Aotenjo takes this to the next level, allowing up to 16 different flower tiles that can trigger unique passive effects when played. Each tile also carries specific keywords, creating interesting synergies with hands for strategic depth.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/17c4958825a64f8b40a18c663dab80a0e328b63f.gif[/img]
For players who love challenges, the current difficulty modes from the demo weren’t enough for some Mahjong veterans. So, we’ve added a new difficulty, featuring four sub-levels for players to conquer.

The EA version will also introduce more than ten new bosses, each with unique mechanics. Here’s a sneak peek at their names: Indeterminate, Inconstant, Immaculate, Invincible, Immortal, Incapable, Inaccessible, Immoral, Insecure, and Inconsiderate. Some old bosses, like Colorless, have also been reworked for a fresh challenge.

[h2]Stay Updated[/h2]
As we approach the final sprint, we’ll be communicating more frequently about things like our future update roadmap and detailed launch plans. Once we finalize the release details, we’ll share them as soon as possible. Don’t forget to [b]add Aotenjo to your wishlist[/b] if you’re interested!

If you have any thoughts or suggestions about this content, feel free to join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/QdvZKhBwme]Discord community[/url] and let us know directly!

Before we wrap up, let’s chat a bit! With the year coming to a close, we’re just as curious as you are about all the game awards going on. Who’s got your vote in this year’s Steam Awards? Let us know in the comments or swing by our [url=https://discord.com/invite/QdvZKhBwme]official Discord[/url] —we’d love to hear your picks!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/cd2151a48b84e829ece4efc25661f2fa5e95f849.png[/img]

Thank you for your support,
Aotenjo Dev Team

notes.title: Development Update of Aotenjo
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!
It's been almost a month since our last demo update, and we've made great strides in developing Aotenjo. We're excited to share some of the latest enhancements with you.

[h3]Introducing the New Deck: Bamboo Bone Mahjong [/h3]
Bamboo Bone Mahjong, inspired by Japanese Mahjong styles, introduces the unique Dora tile mechanism to our game. This new deck not only adds unpredictability but also deepens the strategic play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/0cb29320a4eaea563400fdf493a837b5ec8e582e.png[/img]
Here’s how it works: Indicator tiles and Dora tiles are essential to Riichi Mahjong. Indicator tiles help identify the Dora tiles, which follow them in sequence. For instance, if the indicator tile is the three of characters, the Dora tile will be the four of characters. Simple, right?

In Aotenjo, each game round starts by randomly drawing a Mahjong tile as the indicator. Additional indicator are drawn when a Kong is made, all placed in the indicator area. Scoring big? The successor of the indicator tile—the Dora—will boost your points!

[h3]New Tile Style: Porcelain Tiles[/h3]
Our journey through tiles continues beyond traditional materials like copper and crystal. Drawing from the rich heritage of Chinese porcelain, we've crafted a new set of seven Porcelain tiles. Each tile not only looks stunning but also enhances gameplay with unique effects and the keyword "Appreciate."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45104517/234b0d6af9bb1daec0aceb6d582d1282d6575486.png[/img]
[h3]Ascensions[/h3]
Looking for a challenge? Our ascension modes are here to test your skills. Segmented into four levels—Heaven, Earth, Human, and Goose—each stage is designed to push your strategic limits with varied difficulty settings, score goals, and reward pathways.

We've also broadened the scope of general artifacts and introduced new locations and random starting events, adding layers to your strategic planning.

We're thrilled to announce that Aotenjo will be featured at the Steam Next Fest this October, complete with a brand-new playable demo. Stay tuned for more details!

Join Our Community
For the latest updates and a chance to engage with us directly, don't forget to [url=https://discord.com/invite/QdvZKhBwme]join our official Discord server[/url]!

The Aotenjo Team

notes.title: Q&A:Where we are now and where we are going
notes.content:
This is the main developer and designer of Aotenjo, NonToxicEel, and I’m here to answer some questions you might have:

[h3]Q: Can we play Seven Pairs or Thirteen Orphans?[/h3]
A: Yes, it's possible. Apart from the initial deck, Green Mahjong, the second deck has more available Patterns and special play modes for Seven Pairs and Thirteen Orphans. More special tile patterns and play modes are still under development. Feel free to join the Discord Channel and urge us to update!

[h3]Q: Why does there need to be a Pair for every hand?[/h3]
A: The reason for needing the Pair in the game is that I believe the essence of Mahjong lies in the Pair (also known as the "Head" or  "Eyes"). From the Five-Tiles Mahjong to Taiwanese Mahjong (17 tiles), mahjong's gameplay generally requires some number of Sets plus the Pair. Therefore, if a hand lacks the Pair, it is not a valid Mahjong hand, and the Patterns cannot be assessed.

[h3]Q: Why does it resemble Balatro so much?[/h3]
A: The game indeed draws inspiration from many card-based rogue-like games such as [i]Balatro[/i], [i]Luck be a Landlord[/i], [i]Monster Train[/i], and [i]Slay the Spire[/i], and I do admire the scoring-based challenge game loop created by Balatro. 

However, I believe Aotenjo has the potential to do even better, as it is rooted in the centuries-old traditional game of Mahjong. The richness and beauty of Mahjong tile patterns are, in my opinion, unmatched by other card games. I want to create a game that not only appeals to mahjong players but also introduces and endears non-mahjong players to the game.

[h3]Q: More Accessibility and Multi-platform support?[/h3]
A: We acknowledge that currently the game has issues about accessibility. We are working on several angles to help non-Mahjong players to understand the mechanism of Aotenjo, which includes more tooltips on terminologies, an in-game dictionary and interactive explanations. We are adding a numeral indicator for all the tiles as well, to help players who are not familiar with Mahjong Tiles to have a firmer grasp on the game.

We also heard a lot from Linux and OS X users. Yes, the game will be available on those systems, but it will take time due to a lack of human resources. Controller support is considered, but its priority might not be as high.

[h3]Q: What new content can we expect in the full version?[/h3]
A: There is a lot! First and foremost are new decks: Bamboo Mahjong (with Dora Tiles) and Rainbow Mahjong (with Flower Tiles). Bamboo Mahjong will feature Japanese terminology and more traditional Japanese Pattern, such as Golden Gate Bridge, Benikujaku, and Kokuiisou. Various flower tiles act like special tiles drawn and played immediately, offering unique passive effects in the game. We also have numerous new mechanisms planned, such as the Voided Suit Mechanism, Foreknowledge Mechanism, and more.

Next steps to that are events. We have designed dozens of different events that can bring unexpected changes during gameplay, including acquiring special artifacts, unique tile augments, or instantly losing half of the tiles in the Wall...

Following that are the Puzzle Mode and Weekly Challenges. In normal mode, we might not have found the optimal solution to activate the highest-scoring patterns... But in Puzzle Mode, the goal of each round is to find how to play the tiles to achieve the highest score and overcome one challenge after another!

Finally, there’s the Creative Workshop! Yes! I am a Minecraft modder! Naturally, my game must support mods and texture packs! Custom tile effects, bosses, custom artifacts, quests, skins... whatever you can think of, I've set up interfaces similar to Forge for it!

If you have any questions, bugs, or feedback, feel free to join the Discord Channel.

notes.title: 🀄 Aotenjo - Demo Released! 🀄
notes.content:
Dear Players,

We are thrilled to announce that the highly anticipated Mahjong deckbuilder game [b]Aotenjo [/b]now has a playable demo available! You can download it right now and experience this unique blend of Mahjong and deckbuilding.

[h2]Download the Aotenjo Demo and Get a Peek![/h2]
In this demo, we have included two card decks for you to try out: a beginner’s deck and a standard deck. These decks will allow you to get a taste of Aotenjo's core mechanics, master various Artifacts, Gadgets and Patterns (Yakus), and tackle different malicious threats.

[h3]What's Included in the Demo:[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Beginner’s Deck:[/b] Designed for new players to quickly get up to speed.
[*][b]Standard Deck:[/b] Offers more challenges and variations for experienced players.
[*][b]Dynamic Levels:[/b] Each playthrough generates new Artifacts, gadgets, and augments, providing fresh challenges and fun every time.
[*][b]Endless Mode:[/b] Both decks include an endless mode where players can challenge themselves to achieve even higher scores.
[/list]
[h3]Road to the Full Game[/h3]
In the future full version of Aotenjo, we planned to add many more initial decks for you to choose from and master. You'll be able to explore a wider array of Artifacts, Patterns and Tile Materials, experiencing richer and more varied gameplay. We are excited to grow and develop Aotenjo with you.

[h3]Wishlist and Join Our Discord[/h3]
We warmly invite you to add Aotenjo to your wishlist and [url=https://discord.gg/QdvZKhBwme]join our Discord community[/url]. Your feedback is incredibly valuable to us, whether it's about the game experience or bug reports, it will help us improve and perfect the game.
Thank you for your support of Aotenjo! We can't wait to hear your feedback and see you in the game.

Best regards,
The Aotenjo Development Team
